payload.reason: The evidence indicates that both single-language and multilingual BERT models perform well in capturing syntax-sensitive agreement patterns, but does not provide a definitive conclusion that one outperforms the other across all contexts.

claims.text: Single-language BERT performs well on structure-dependent agreement tasks, achieving above 80% accuracy in cloze tests.
Multilingual BERT also captures syntax-sensitive agreement patterns, but the evidence does not clearly state it outperforms single-language BERT.
BERT's performance varies by language and task, suggesting that comparisons between single-language and multilingual models may be context-dependent.
